# OA v0.7.24

**Status:** Public development preview

**Release date:** 2026-08-29

**Source:** [`v0.7.24`](https://github.com/realminc/oa/releases/tag/v0.7.24)

## Summary

OA v0.7.24 establishes the native Vulkan Video decode and presentation
foundation. It publishes exact codec-profile admission, pinned 8/10-bit
conformance media, native P010 paths, capability-gated hardware sampler-YCbCr
conversion, stable frame stepping and reverse playback, and reproducible
1080p60/UHD60 qualification for H.264, H.265, AV1, and VP9.

## Added and improved

- Exact profile, chroma, depth, level, tier, and native-format queries replace
  extension-only codec admission.
- H.264 Baseline/Main/High 8-bit 4:2:0; H.265 Main 8, Main 10, and qualified
  Range Extensions 8/10-bit 4:2:0; AV1 Main 8 and a fail-closed Main 10 subset;
  and VP9 Profiles 0/2 are fixture-backed on the qualified Intel device.
- Hardware sampler-YCbCr conversion is the default when its exact format,
  sampler, queue, descriptor, and lifetime contract is supported. The compute
  route remains the validated fallback and explicit comparison path.
- Bounded decode-ahead and presentation caching provide exact single-frame
  forward/backward stepping and smooth held-key reverse traversal.
- Checked-in 720p correctness, 1080p60 baseline, and UHD60 qualification clips
  carry source provenance, regeneration commands, hashes, and manifest data.
- Video product code, tutorials, conformance tests, FFmpeg differential
  harnesses, and benchmarks now use OA-owned foundation types. Raw process and
  `FILE*` calls remain only at the external FFmpeg oracle seam.

## Compatibility and migration

No stable public API is removed in this patch. Video remains capability-gated:
applications must treat `Unavailable` as an honest device/profile result and
must not infer support from extension presence alone. Rebuild native consumers
and discard pre-1.0 binary, pipeline, execution-plan, and media-session caches.

The root quick start now checks `oa::print(...).isOk()`; `oa::puts` is not part
of the OA formatting surface.

## Performance

On the qualified Intel Iris Xe TGL GT2 / Mesa 26.1.7 host, every measured
1080p60 and UHD60 decode/present process exceeded the 60 fps source cadence
with zero CPU pixel readback; the slowest UHD process reached 198.771 fps.
UHD AV1 hardware/manual YCbCr conversion reached qualified parity in both
execution orders. The remaining ratios are characterization because laptop
thermal spread exceeded the 15% promotion gate. Full provenance, per-process
ranges, and reproduction commands are in the
[video benchmark](../benchmarks/oaVideo.md).

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| Native decoder contract | Release 41/41 |
| Independent FFmpeg differential | Release 6/6; every checked frame above the 30 dB corruption gate |
| Host memory safety | ASAN/LSAN 41/41 + 6/6; UBSAN 41/41 + 6/6 |
| Vulkan validation | Core and synchronization validation clean; focused GPU-assisted route clean apart from expected layer configuration warnings |
| Exact capability matrix | 26 legal codec/profile/chroma/depth requests recorded on the qualified device |
| Realtime benchmark contract | Correctness regexes, exact assets, fresh processes, cooldown, thermal gate, and zero readback enforced |

## Known limitations

- H.265 Main Still Picture is still fixture-gated: the installed x265 maps its
  advertised selection to Range Extensions profile IDC 4, and QSV cannot
  initialize a genuine IDC-3 stream on the current `xe` stack.
- H.264 High 4:4:4; H.265 4:2:2/4:4:4/12-bit/SCC; AV1 High/Professional; and
  VP9 Profiles 1/3 are unsupported by the qualified TGL device and remain
  unverified rather than synthetically admitted.
- AV1 Main 10 loop restoration fails closed before submission pending a
  qualified implementation.
- UHD60 H.264 exceeds this device's reported H.264 level ceiling; UHD VP9 is
  rejected by its exact capability query. H.265/AV1 provide the qualified UHD
  decode routes on this host.
- H.265 encode remains blocked by a reproduced TGL/Mesa device-loss defect;
  broader encode and cross-vendor qualification require additional hardware.

## Upgrade

Rebuild OA and native consumers, regenerate owned bindings and examples, and
discard stale binary, pipeline, graph, and video-session caches. Keep runtime
codec/profile checks enabled and use the compute color-conversion route only
as the explicit fallback or diagnostic comparator.
